probes.summary:
ANSWER: YES — the permutation fast-mode default breaks esttab-class table tools, in the SILENT_WRONG sense specifically. No tool in the family ever refuses: every one of the 19 probes returned rc 0. "Breaks" therefore resolves entirely to silent misreporting, in the console, in .tex, and in .csv.

(1) THE HEADLINE. `esttab fast anal, se star` prints two columns with digit-for-digit identical coefficients; column (1) (fast mode) has a completely blank SE row and no stars, column (2) (analytic) has (0.0630) and `***`. Nothing between the command and the table says why. A reader compares them and concludes the permutation estimate is insignificant. The footer still reads "Standard errors in parentheses" and the legend still reads "* p<0.05, ** p<0.01, *** p<0.001" — both assertions are false for column (1). I grepped the fast-mode probe output for warning text: the only hits are esttab's routine "(file ... not found)" notice from `replace`, unrelated to the VCV. There is no warning of any kind. Same pattern in fast.tex (SE rows are `            &                     \\`, footnote `\textit{t} statistics in parentheses`) and fast.csv (`="",=""` cells under a `="t statistics in parentheses"` row). Plain `estout` (cells(b) only) and `eststo` are CLEAN — nothing SE-dependent is requested, nothing is missing.

(2) THE AUTHOR'S PROPOSED REMEDY, MEASURED — and it does not do what it is meant to. I synthesized the all-zero e(V) state with `ereturn post e(b) J(6,6,0)` and ran esttab on it. Zero V is NOT transparently false to these tools. It changes blank to `(.)` for se/t/p — marginally more visible, but the footer and star legend still assert statistics that are not there, so the grade does not improve. And on the `ci` path it is strictly worse: `esttab ., ci` prints `[0.824,0.824]`, `[-0.0457,-0.0457]` — fabricated zero-width confidence intervals that look like real, infinitely precise numbers. `_se[main_att]` also returns `0` with rc 0, so Stata's own accessor reports a zero SE rather than refusing. The all-zero matrix trades one silent failure for a new fabrication.

(3) A REMEDY THAT DOES WORK, MEASURED. estout reads posted `e(se)`/`e(p)`/`e(t)`/`e(ci_l)`/`e(ci_u)` directly, ahead of computing them from e(V) (estout.ado ComputeCoefs 3169-3173). Posting `e(se)` and `e(p)` from quantities wooldid ALREADY has in e() made `esttab ., se star` render (0.130), (0.0767)... and `esttab ., p` render (0.095), (0.857)... correctly, with no e(V) posted at all and rc 0. This is the one route measured to produce a correct, non-fabricated table.

(4) The permutation p-values sit in e() the entire time — `e(perm_p)` is a 1x6 matrix reading .0952381, .85714286, .85714286, .47619048, .0952381, .0952381 — and no default table writer surfaces any of them.

(5) One constraint on implementing any V remedy: `ereturn repost V =` on a b-only estimate refuses with rc 503 "conformability error". A V (or the aux matrices) must be supplied at post time, not bolted on afterwards.

CAVEATS. The zero-V and posted-aux findings are synthetic — I constructed the posted-results state from outside wooldid; I am READ-ONLY on the repo and changed nothing. The fresh `ereturn post` for the zero-V block drops e(df_r) and wooldid's other e(), which does not move the result (se=. gives t=. regardless of df; se=0 gives [b,b] regardless of critical value) but is stated for completeness. Every e(perm_p) in this fixture is >= .0952, so zero stars is CORRECT in the posted-aux probes and star rendering from e(p) is not exercised. `e(perm_se_shift)` was my arbitrary choice of permutation SE for the probe; which SE (if any) is the right one to post is the author's call, as is whether `e(perm_ci)` should feed `e(ci_l)`/`e(ci_u)` (a source-only observation I did not run).

probes.summary: The permutation fast-mode default DOES break esttab-class table tools, in the worst way available: nothing errors, everything renders, and the permutation column is silently stripped of its inference. Across every esttab variant tried (default/se/ci/p/t/wide/nostar/stats, mixed and all-permutation, screen and file) the return code was 0 and the table printed the fast-mode coefficients with an empty parenthesis cell and NO STARS. Decisive exhibit (pB.log, 200 reps): e(perm_p) = .00995 for main_att, ES_att_post0 and ES_att_post1, yet esttab prints "main_att 0.824" starless in the permutation column beside an identical "0.824***" in the analytic column, under the shared footer "* p<0.05, ** p<0.01, *** p<0.001". The star suppression is therefore not a coincidence of this dataset's p-value — estout has no p-value at all, so no coefficient can ever earn a star in fast mode regardless of how strong the randomization-inference evidence is. The all-permutation table (both columns fast mode) is the cleanest exhibit: esttab prints the footer "Standard errors in parentheses" over a table containing zero parenthesized values. The defect exports intact: mixed.tex is publication-ready LaTeX with "0.824\sym{***}" in column 1, bare "0.824" in column 2, an empty SE cell, and the p<0.05 legend as a \multicolumn footnote. MECHANISM (estout.ado L3050-3070): estout tries "capt mat tmp = vecdiag(e(V))"; on failure it falls back to "capt confirm mat e(se)"; when both fail it does "mat bc = bc, J(rowsof(bc),1,.y)" and CONTINUEs — .y is estout's internal "vacant" marker, rendered as the empty vacant string at L1601. No message, no rc, no note. estout never reads e(properties) (zero grep hits in estout.ado and esttab.ado), so wooldid's correct declaration e(properties)="b" is invisible to it — there is no hook by which estout could notice. THE ACCESSORIES THEMSELVES ARE ALL CLEAN. eststo, estimates dir, estadd (scalar, local, matrix, beta, summ), eststo clear, estimates store/restore and estimates save/use all return rc 0 on a fast-mode estimate, and — importantly for the author — e(V)'s absence survives every round trip faithfully: after restore and after use-from-disk, "confirm matrix e(V)" is still r(111), e(wdid_vcvstate) is still "absent", e(perm_p_att) and e(b) are intact, and _se[main_att] still refuses with "_se not allowed when e(V) is not present". estadd does not conjure an e(V). estpost refuses wooldid with "invalid subcommand" r(198) identically for fast mode, permanalyticse and plain no-permute wooldid, so that is an unsupported-subcommand refusal and out of scope for this question. ON THE PROPOSED REMEDY — I measured both candidates rather than guessing, and NEITHER satisfies both halves of the author's criterion ("lets those tools run" AND "transparently false to anyone who inspects it"). (1) An all-zero e(V) does NOT close the star gap: it renders "0.824" starless exactly as today, changing only the parenthesis cell from blank to "(.)", while flipping _se[main_att] from a loud r(111) refusal to a silent fabricated 0 that downstream code will consume without complaint. It buys a visible marker in the table at the cost of a fabricated number in the programmatic path. (2) Posting a matrix literally named e(se) hits estout's own documented fallback and makes the family work completely — se, t, ci and STARS all populate for the permutation column — while e(V) stays absent so _se[] still correctly errors r(111). But the stars it produces come from a t=b/se normal approximation, not from the randomization-inference p-values, so the column then looks fully inferenced: it satisfies "tools run" and fails "transparently false". Reporting both as measured tradeoffs, not as recommendations. probes.summary:
VERDICT: YES, the permutation fast-mode default breaks Stata's own table tools, and it breaks them loudly in most places but silently in one that matters.

Grading rule used: worst_grade is computed over FAST-MODE-ATTRIBUTABLE findings only. predict, margins, estimates replay and estat summarize fail (or degrade) IDENTICALLY on the analytic controls, so they are recorded honestly but excluded from the verdict. All three configurations were re-verified in this session: fast mode gives e(properties)=|b|, e(vce)=||, e(vcetype)=||, e(wdid_vcvstate)=|absent|, `confirm matrix e(V)` rc=111; the permanalyticse and no-permute controls both give e(properties)=|b V|, e(vce)=|cluster|, e(vcetype)=|Robust|, rc=0.

THE HEADLINE (HARD_ERROR). `estimates table` refuses with r(321) "FAST estimation results do not have e(b) and e(V)" in EVERY form tested: live, named, bare, ,se, ,star, ,b se t p, and with stats(). The bare coefficient-only table - which needs no variance at all - refuses too, and the error message is itself inaccurate since e(b) exists. Critically, one fast-mode model anywhere in a multi-model namelist kills the WHOLE table including the columns for models that do have e(V): `estimates table FAST PLAIN, star`, `PLAIN FAST`, `FAST APERM, se` and `FAST APERM PLAIN, stats(N r2)` all returned r(321) and printed nothing, while the all-analytic control `estimates table APERM PLAIN, star` printed a full starred two-column table. That is the built-in analogue of the mixed esttab table, and it is exactly the workflow the author is worried about. test, lincom, nlcom (r(321)), estat vce (r(322)) and _se[] (r(111)) also refuse loudly and correctly. The r(321) gate is Stata-generic - it reproduces on a hand-built b-only `ereturn post` of a regress e(b) with no wooldid involved - so it is not something wooldid is doing wrong beyond declining to post a matrix.

THE SILENT ONE (SILENT_WRONG, and the reason worst_grade is not HARD_ERROR). `estimates stats FAST PLAIN` runs rc=0 and prints FAST with df=0, AIC 801.8202, BIC 801.8202 beside PLAIN's df=6, AIC 813.8202, BIC 843.0218 - the same fit, the same log likelihood, the same 6 parameters. It derives df from rank(e(V)) and assumes rank 0. It does print "(FAST does not contain matrix e(V); rank = 0 assumed)", but that note does not say the IC columns are invalid, and the table it heads shows the permute() run apparently BEATING its own analytic twin on both criteria. Nothing is omitted or blanked; the SE-dependent cells are filled with fabricated values. A user doing model selection off that table picks the wrong row.

WHAT SURVIVES CLEANLY. `estimates store` + `estimates restore` + bare `wooldid` replay is the best-behaved consumer measured: rc=0, the full wooldid table with a blank se_analytic column, and an explicit footer - "No analytic standard errors were computed (the permute() fast-mode default; permanalyticse restores them), so the se_analytic and t_perm columns are blank and no e(V) or e(V_es_*) is posted." `estimates dir` is also clean (FAST listed with 6 params, indistinguishable from the controls). `ereturn display` is DEGRADED_LOUD: it drops the SE/t/p/CI columns entirely rather than blanking them, which is unmistakable.

ONE WOOLDID-SIDE WART, FIXABLE REGARDLESS OF THE ARTIFICIAL-V DECISION. `ereturn display` under fast mode prints the header "(Std. err. adjusted for 80 clusters in i)" above a table that has no standard errors. wooldid's PS-1 block clears e(vce) and e(vcetype) when no V is posted but leaves e(N_clust)=80 and e(clustvar)="i" (all four re-verified), and _coef_table prints the cluster note off those. Clearing N_clust/clustvar too - or accepting the line - is an independent call.

THE REMEDY, MEASURED NOT OPINED. I simulated the author's proposal by re-posting e(b) with a 6x6 all-zero V inside an e-class helper (`ereturn post` accepted it unaltered; `matrix list e(V)` shows every cell exactly 0; note that `ereturn repost V=` CANNOT be used - it needs a conformable existing e(V) and returns r(503) when e(V) is absent, so this must be done at post time). Result: every probed tool runs, rc=0 across the board, and each HARD_ERROR converts into a SILENT_WRONG of the blank-SE / no-star kind. `estimates table ZEROV PLAIN, star` prints a clean two-column table in which the ZEROV column is visually IDENTICAL to a column of genuinely insignificant coefficients - no stars, no marker, no footnote. `estimates table, se` prints a literal 0 in the SE cell; `ereturn display` prints `.` for SE/t/p/CI; `_se[main_att]` returns 0 with rc=0 instead of erroring, so downstream b/se code divides by zero silently. `test` is the loudest survivor ("Constraint 1 dropped", F(0,79)=.), and `estat vce` printing a matrix of exact zeros is the one place the falsity really is transparent on inspection. And there is a strict regression: `estimates stats ZEROV PLAIN` LOSES the "(does not contain matrix e(V); rank = 0 assumed)" note - because e(V) now exists the check is skipped - while df=0 and AIC 801.8203 persist. So the artificial matrix removes the only warning that command currently emits.

Net for the ruling: the fast-mode default does break esttab-class table tools, decisively and in the multi-model case. An all-zero e(V) does let them all run. But "transparently false to anyone who inspects it" holds only for estat vce and the b/se legend; the starred mixed table - the artefact users actually paste into a paper - does not invite inspection and reads as a well-estimated null. The trade is loud-refusal-now for quiet-zero-SE-later, plus the loss of estimates stats' warning. If the artificial V is adopted, the mixed-table indistinguishability and the estat ic note loss are the two things worth compensating for elsewhere (e.g. keeping e(vce)/e(vcetype) cleared so no "Robust" label appears, and a standing footer disclosure).

Simulated faithfully (vce/vcetype left cleared, e(properties)="b V"), the all-zero V makes coefplot STOP printing its warning and emit ll==ul==b with se==0 — a fabricated degenerate interval whose rendered PNG is pixel-indistinguishable from the honest no-interval plot; makes `estimates table, b se` print an SE column of literal 0s under a "b/se" legend; makes `estimates table, b star` and `putexcel = etable` silently strip every significance star that the analytic control shows (control writes " .82352847***" to Excel, zero-V writes "0.82352847"); makes `ereturn display` print blank SE/t/p/CI cells under live column headers; and makes `_se[main_att]` return 0 with rc=0 so a hand-rolled `abs(_b/_se)>1.96` is FALSE for every coefficient (today that same expression hard-errors r(111)). remedy.verdict:
THE REMEDY FAILS ITS OWN PRECONDITION, AND ON NET IT INCREASES SILENT MISREPORTING. Recommend: do not post the all-zero matrix.

1. IT UNBLOCKS NOTHING IN THE ESTTAB CLASS, BECAUSE NOTHING THERE WAS BLOCKED. The author's condition was to post a fake V "that lets those tools run". My fast-mode control shows every estout-family probe ALREADY runs with no e(V) at all: esttab bare, esttab se star, esttab ci, esttab p, estout cells(b(star) se), esttab->.tex and esttab->.csv all returned rc=0 with nothing posted. The zero matrix's entire effect on that family is to change a blank cell to "(.)" - and, for ci, to change a blank cell into a fabricated number. The false footers ("Standard errors in parentheses", "95% confidence intervals in brackets", "* p<0.05, ** p<0.01, *** p<0.001") are untouched in both states.

2. WHAT IT ACTUALLY UNBLOCKS IS STATA'S BUILT-INS, AND THERE THE TRANSITION IS MOSTLY HARD_ERROR -> SILENT_WRONG. On a 23-probe basis (excluding the rc=198 syntax row, which fails identically on the analytic control): SILENT_WRONG goes from 7 to 16; HARD_ERROR goes from 12 to 0; DEGRADED_LOUD 3 -> 4; CLEAN 1 -> 3. Twelve loud, accurate refusals are converted into runs, and eight of those twelve become silent misreports (_se[] -> "0"; estimates table b se -> a literal "0" SE; estimates table b t p; lincom x2, which also hand callers r(se)=0; nlcom; plus ereturn display and r(table) losing their honest reduced shape). Only four of the twelve land somewhere defensible: test x3 degrade loudly ("Constraint 1 dropped", F(0,79)=.), and estat vce/matrix list e(V) become genuinely clean inspection surfaces.

3. TWO SURFACES GET STRICTLY WORSE - THESE ARE THE FINDINGS I'D PUT IN FRONT OF THE AUTHOR. (a) esttab ., ci turns a blank into "[0.824,0.824]", "[-0.0457,-0.0457]" - fabricated zero-width confidence intervals that read as real, infinitely precise estimates. (b) coefplot loses its warning: fast mode prints "(.: could not determine CI1)" and draws no whiskers; with the zero V there is no notice at all and it silently draws zero-width whiskers. In both cases the artificial matrix replaces a visible absence with a confident-looking falsehood - the exact SILENT_WRONG outcome the grading scheme calls the worst.

4. THE MATRIX IS NOT "TRANSPARENTLY FALSE TO ANYONE WHO INSPECTS IT" - the ruling's own condition is not met. Only 2 of the 24 surfaces show the zeros: "matrix list e(V)" and "estat vce". The canonical inspection command, ereturn list, shows only "e(V) :  6 x 6" - dimensions, never contents - while e(vce) and e(vcetype) are empty and the honest marker e(wdid_vcvstate)="absent" is a hidden macro that ereturn list does not print. Worse, the posted zero surfaces itself in THREE mutually inconsistent renderings, so a reader cannot even learn one tell: a literal "0" (_se[], estimates table b se, lincom's r(se), coefplot x_se), a "." (ereturn display, esttab se/p, estout, r(table)'s se row), and a point-width interval equal to the coefficient (esttab ci, coefplot ll1/ul1). The falseness is visible only to someone who already knew to look. Adding a visible label (e(vcetype)="ARTIFICIAL") fixes ereturn display and ereturn list but provably reaches nothing in estout - esttab ci still prints "[0.824,0.824]".

5. IT ALSO COSTS MORE TO BUILD THAN THE ruling ASSUMES. "ereturn repost V=" cannot be used: it returns rc=503 "conformability error" on fast mode because there is no existing e(V) to replace (rc=0 on the permanalyticse state, which is why the package's bootstrap path can use it). A real fix must post b and the artificial V together at the original post site and then restore the ~40 e() entries that ereturn post wipes.

BOTTOM LINE FOR THE RULING: on the author's stated test - "if it does not break them, leave as is" - the esttab-class tools do not refuse under fast mode, so the "lets those tools run" rationale does not apply to them; and where the remedy does change behaviour it converts loud refusals into silent fabrication and makes two surfaces strictly worse. Leaving e(V) absent is the safer of the two states measured. If the author nonetheless wants something posted, the properties-without-V variant is the least bad of the posted options (it keeps 5 built-in refusals loud, including Stata's own rc=322 naming the inconsistency) but it still fabricates the esttab CIs and ships a state Stata regards as malformed. The only route measured to produce a CORRECT table remains the one from the prior probe - posting e(se)/e(p) from the permutation quantities wooldid already holds in e(perm_p) etc., which estout reads ahead of e(V).
